questions.stem: For data set 3383, find the bug: switch(x){case 1: y=1; case 2: y=2; break;} what is wrong?

options.misconception: Missing break lets execution continue into the next case
Incorrectly assumed switch requires a non-integer selector
Confused an optional default with a required clause

options.text: The condition must be a range
options.misconception: Mistook switch matching for interval comparison

questions.explanation: Option A is the key because the first case has no break, so execution falls through into the second case and overwrites y Option B fails because switch selectors can be integer expressions in C Option C fails because the default label is optional, not required Option D fails because switch matches discrete case labels, not ranges.
questions.hint: Look for a case group that lacks a terminating break statement.

questions.stem: For data set 3384, find the bug: if (x = 5) { puts("yes"); } what is wrong?

options.misconception: A single equals sign stores a value instead of testing it
Misread a nonzero assignment as a false truth value
Confused a comparison bug with a declaration error
Mistook a logic error for a syntax error

questions.explanation: Option A is the key because the single equals sign assigns five to x and then tests that nonzero value as true, so the condition never compares Option B fails because a nonzero assignment is treated as true, not false Option C fails because x is declared elsewhere; this is a logic error Option D fails because the statement is syntactically complete; the fault is logical.
questions.hint: Comparisons use a doubled operator, not a single equals sign.

questions.stem: For data set 3387, a film studio averages the readings 5, 7, 9; what mean is printed?
questions.explanation: The mean is the sum of the readings divided by their count. Adding 5, 7, and 9 gives 21, and dividing by three yields 7. Remember that dividing by the number of readings, not by the largest one, produces the mean.
questions.hint: Add all readings and divide by how many there are.

questions.explanation: Repeating 7 items across 4 equal rows gives 7 times 4 = 28 cells. Multiplication counts equal groups, so the total is the group size multiplied by the number of groups.

questions.stem: For data set 3390, an array holds 19 elements; what is the index of its final element?
questions.explanation: C arrays are zero-indexed, so an array of 19 elements uses indices 0 through 18. The last index is one less than the element count, a classic off-by-one boundary that new programmers often miss.
questions.hint: Remember that indexing starts at zero, not one.

questions.stem: For data set 3391, a observatory records the remainder when 81 is divided by 6; what value is printed?
questions.explanation: The remainder operator gives what is left after dividing 81 by 6. Since 6 fits into 81 a whole number of times with 3 left over, the printed value is 3. Integer division alone would give the quotient instead.
questions.hint: Find the leftover after dividing evenly, not the quotient.

questions.explanation: The loop continues while i is strictly less than 5. Starting from 0, i takes the values 0 through 4, which is 5 distinct iterations. The strict less-than condition excludes 5 itself, so the count equals the bound.
questions.hint: Count the integer values that satisfy the strict inequality.

questions.stem: For data set 3393, an engineer computes the C expression 5 << 2; what integer results?
questions.explanation: Shifting an integer left by two bit positions multiplies it by four. Therefore 5 << 2 equals 5 times 4, which is 20. A right shift would divide instead, and adding two would be a different operation entirely.
questions.hint: A left shift by n multiplies by two to the power of n.

questions.stem: For data set 3394, a program prints the integer quotient of 144 divided by 7; what appears?
questions.explanation: When both operands are integers, C division discards the fractional part. Dividing 144 by 7 gives a quotient of 20 after truncation. A floating-point divisor would preserve the fraction and give a different result.
questions.hint: Truncate the fractional part of the division result.
